speaker: (UI)
current_text: The Capital: the walls are up and the Approved Gate is the only way in. Pass Captain Spotless's entry examination (a card battle), or find another way.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: HP does not come back after battles; rifts hurt; the hideout heals. {villain}'s Castle waits at the far end of the city.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: You are inside the Capital. Find the hideout (the manhole near the gate), help the Wrinkles (one quest per Path), seal the rifts you can and reach {villain}'s Castle at the north end. Each Path you free mends one of the city's broken services.
new_text: Find the hideout through the manhole near the gate. Help the Wrinkles, one quest per Path; seal rifts and reach {villain}'s Castle at the north end. Each freed Path mends a broken city service.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: The Capital is free. The facade is down, the rifts are closed and the citizens are saying whatever they like, mostly to each other. The Crease is open to everybody.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Walk back down the road to {town}?

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Leaving the Capital ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The Approved Gate stays open for you, but every roaming officer, inspector and Tidy-Bot will be back next time, and so will the rifts.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Leaving the Capital ends this visit. Town heals you fully. Nobody will ask for your exit permit. Nobody has a permit machine. The road is just a road.

current_text: The Entry Examination

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Captain Spotless measures you against the Approved Visitor Standard: a hard card battle, his deck fair to nobody. Your HP carries in from the zone and nothing heals in between. Lose, and you wake outside, a little poorer.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Take the examination

speaker: (UI)
current_text: {villain}'s Castle

speaker: (UI)
current_text: The great doors stand open, which is worse than closed. Twenty-odd rooms of portraits and good intentions, then {villain} himself. HP carries in; nothing heals except at the shrines. Your zone's broken-service debuffs apply to every duel.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: {villain} is gone. The castle is just a very large, very tidy building now, and the portraits have started to peel. You may walk through it again for the memories (and the gold). HP carries in; nothing heals except at the shrines.

speaker: (UI)
current_text: Enter the castle

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The doors of {villain}'s Castle are made of gold, and every handle has been polished until it shows you your own worried face. Beyond them: a long gallery, a smell of floor wax, and the sound of someone very pleased with himself, humming.
new_text: You see your worried face in the gold handles of {villain}'s Castle. Beyond the doors, you smell floor wax and hear someone humming.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The doors of {villain}'s Castle stand open. The gold is flaking. A pigeon has built a nest in the crown above the lintel and nobody has asked it for a permit.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Nurse Hesper hands you a cup of the Tea of Dissent. It is strong, bitter and entirely unapproved. HP restored.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You are already at full HP. Nurse Hesper hands you a cup anyway. 'Dissent,' she says, 'is good for the circulation.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Ow! The Capital has hurt you again. (-HP)

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: You wake up on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray is writing on a clipboard that, you notice, is blank on purpose.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: 'Dragged you in by the collar. Correction fee is on you; the Wrinkles run on small coins and large grudges. Drink your tea.'
new_text: 'Dragged you in by the collar. Correction fee is yours. Drink. Then we can discuss your habit of arriving unconscious.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: You wake up on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray is writing on a clipboard. It says 'NOTES', and then, in small letters, 'finally'.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. The fee is on you, still; the tea is not free just because the kingdom is.'
new_text: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. Fee is yours. Drink the tea while it is hot; freedom hasn't changed that part.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: You wake up in the dust outside the Approved Gate, under a sign that says STAND HERE. A guard is leaning over you, measuring your height with a long stick.
new_text: You wake in the dust outside the Approved Gate. A guard leans over you, measuring your height with a long stick.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
current_text: 'Fell over in the approved queue area. That is a minor offence: a fine. Please stand up to the approved height. You have shrunk, citizen.'
new_text: 'Falling in the approved queue area: minor offence. Fine payable. Stand up, citizen. I cannot measure you along the ground.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A hidden stash! Someone hid this where {villain}'s inspectors would not look: behind something untidy.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You are through the walls. Somewhere a loudspeaker clears its throat. You are now, officially, a Visitor in {capital}, the Capital of {kingdom}.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The service-tunnel network is down. Nobody has run the wheels that power the shaft lifts in ten years. 'No travel,' says a Wrinkle's note on the hatch.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'Free the Gainlands and we will get the lifts turning.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You drop down the shaft, ride the lift through the dark and climb out somewhere else, smelling of rust.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You climb the ladder and push the manhole open. The Capital's cold light falls in.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You crawl out through the old tunnel and push the rubble aside. The Outskirts again, and a long way from anybody's approved queue.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You squeeze back down the collapsed shaft and follow the old tunnel in the dark.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You push through a gap between rubble and a toppled statue. Behind it: stairs, a smell of damp brick, and an old plaque in four different handwritings: 'THE OLD JOINT WORKS. BUILT BY ALL FOUR PATHS, TOGETHER, BACK WHEN WE DID THAT.'
new_text: You push past rubble and a toppled statue. You find stairs and read an old plaque: 'THE OLD JOINT WORKS. BUILT BY ALL FOUR PATHS, TOGETHER.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The tunnel runs under the wall, under the gate and under every one of {villain}'s checkpoints. You walk under them all. It is the best moment you have had all day.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You knock three times. The manhole opens to a hand and a tired voice: 'Down you come.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A manhole by the wall, with a scratch on its lid like a tiny wrinkle. You knock three times, for no reason you can name.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A pause. Then the lid lifts and a hand beckons. A voice mutters, 'Wrinkle?' You decide that, yes, you are.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Down a ladder, along a brick tunnel, into a warm room full of mismatched furniture and people who are all, visibly, not ironed.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You scribble a moustache on His Perfection. It improves him enormously. A small coin falls out of the frame: somebody in the Wrinkles pays a bounty on moustaches.
new_text: You draw a moustache on {villain_title}'s portrait. A small coin drops from the frame: the Wrinkles' bounty for this improvement.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Already improved. He has a moustache now. He looks, for the first time, like a person.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You post a complaint. A slot opens and, impossibly, a small coin falls out with a note: 'Thank you for your feedback. Here is a small sum for your inconvenience. Do not complain again.'
new_text: You post a complaint. A coin drops from a slot with a note: 'Compensation for your inconvenience. Please use it to have less inconvenience.'
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You post a complaint. A hatch opens and a warm cup of tea is pushed out, still steaming. 'We value your concern,' says a note. You feel a little better.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You post a complaint. Nothing happens. The box says, in a very gentle voice: 'Your complaint has been noted.' You have never felt so unnoted.
new_text: You post a complaint. 'Noted,' says the box, gently. You wait. That appears to have been the whole service.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You post a complaint. A klaxon sounds. A Perfection Inspector appears from nowhere, measures your frown, writes you up and walks off.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'Thank you for your feedback,' says the box.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The box rattles. It is full. It has had enough of your feedback for one visit.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You set the rift-stone and say the old word: close. The tear shudders, folds in on itself like a letter, and is gone. The air smells of rain. Sealed!

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The rift-stone will not take while the rift's guardian still stands. Whatever it spat out has to go first.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The rift is sealed. Where it was there is a scorch mark and the memory of a very bad idea.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: This one is too big. It runs all the way up into the castle. It will have to close when he does.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A real recipe, written by hand, with a stain of actual sauce on the corner! A pinch of this, a spoonful of that. It is wonderfully imprecise. You tuck it away.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A banished compost heap, hiding in a cellar where it was not allowed to be. It is warm. It is alive.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: It steams, very slightly, with gratitude. Rescued!

speaker: (narration)
current_text: A rubber stamp the size of your fist, the handle worn smooth. FINAL APPROVAL, it reads, in letters that have been inked a thousand times. Someone has wrapped it in a handkerchief and hidden it here, in case the world needed it.
new_text: You unwrap a handkerchief and find a worn rubber stamp: FINAL APPROVAL. Someone hid it here, ready for the day it was needed.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: An old glass jar with one seed in it. The seed is glowing very faintly green. Nobody has planted anything in the Capital for ten years. It has not given up.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You already took the one lying here.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: There is nothing here.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The crew of the first wheel keeps running while you talk, because stopping is not permitted. 'Cardio,' pants a woman, 'is mandatory.' You find the brake lever under a pile of notices.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The wheel groans, slows and stops. The crew sit on the floor and laugh and cry at the same time.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The second wheel has been turning since before some of its runners were old enough to vote. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You take it off its hook and put it in your pocket.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The wheel winds down. 'We were told,' says a man, 'that this was how you got strong.'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The third wheel's crew are children. Children! 'It is a school activity,' says a banner.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You pull the lever, break the wheel's rhythm and get them off. They are very small and very proud and they will not stop saying 'Rollo sent you?'.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: This crew is free. They are lying on the ground, looking at the sky. It is the best they have felt in ten years.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You cut the big black cable that feeds the facade's lights from the wheels. A spark; a silence. Far off, the perfect lamps flicker, stutter and come back on: {villain} keeps a very small private generator, just for himself.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The cable is cut. The wires twitch occasionally, out of habit.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You pull the lever and ask the Perfect Nutrient Paste Dispenser for a refund. It chokes, burps and covers itself in a bright green foam that smells, fatally, of actual cabbage. A paste machine is not supposed to remember cabbage.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The dispenser is spoiled and sulking. The foam is still fizzing a little.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: With the Stamp of Final Approval pressed to the form, the grave plot's little iron gate unlocks. A line of mourners, who have waited three years outside, file in.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Mr. Pell, in a coffin carried by the whole neighbourhood, is laid to rest at last. Somebody plays a very small, very sad, very real tune.
new_text: You watch the neighbourhood carry Mr. Pell to his grave. A quiet tune accompanies the coffin as they lower it.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Pell plot is tended and quiet. Fresh flowers. The family comes every morning now.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The iron gate is sealed with a notice: 'NO BURIAL WITHOUT A STAMPED PERMIT (FORM 27-B/6, FINAL APPROVAL).' You have no stamp. Widow Pell said something about a stamp, hidden somewhere in Grave Row.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You kneel, scoop a hole with your hands and drop in the seed. You water it with what is left in your flask. Nothing happens, for one long, bad moment.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Then a shoot, as thin as a thread, noses out of the dirt. And another. And a flower, the colour of everything the Capital is not.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The patch is green and growing. A bee, which should not exist in the Capital, hovers over it, deciding.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The patch is sick, grey and cracked, and nothing will grow in it without a seed. Old Fern mentioned an old seed in a jar, hidden somewhere in the Reek.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The clerk behind the window slides you a form. 'For a burial permit, Form 27-B. Please attach Form 27-C (Proof of Grief).'

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You ask for 27-C. 'Please attach Form 27-B,' she says.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'Form 27-C requires Form 27-B.' 'Form 27-B requires Form 27-C.' 'It is a loop,' you say.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'It is a process,' she says, with fear in her eyes.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'Please take a number.' You take a number. It says 4,112,009.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The sign above the window says NOW SERVING: 3. It has said so for three years.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: 'Spontaneity Permits are issued on Thursdays, between 3 and 3:05, by appointment,' says the sign. The clerk inside has been asleep, upright, with her eyes open, since the last Thursday.
new_text: You read: 'Spontaneity Permits: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05, by appointment.' Inside, the clerk sleeps upright, eyes open.
writer_note: Character-specific wording; preserves the existing beat and facts.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Blackout

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Beefcakes kept the kingdom's energy and its roads: the wheels, the mills, the throwers and the portal-rippers. {villain} put them all on wheels to light one small town. The rest of the kingdom went dark.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The lights are back on: the street lamps burn, the lifts run, the tunnels are open again, and the Beefcakes' wheels, free at last, turn for everyone.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Famine

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Gourmands fed and guarded the kingdom. {villain} replaced them with Perfect Nutrient Paste. Real food is gone from the Capital, and so is the comfort it gave.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The food stalls have reopened: awnings, steam, lanterns, real food. Healing items work again, and the stomachs of the Capital are not quite so empty.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Restless Dead

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Necrocrats looked after the dead and their paperwork. {villain}'s permits locked the dead out of their graves and the paperwork in an endless loop. The dead do not rest, and the things that have died keep coming back.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The cemetery is calm: graves are tended, the permit loop has been broken, and the dead are finally allowed to lie down.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Clutter

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Refusemancers took out the kingdom's waste and turned it back into soil. {villain} called composting untidy and hid the garbage behind the facade. Rubbish is piling up, in the streets and in your deck.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The heaps are smaller and greener. Things are being composted again and the Reek smells, very faintly, of flowers.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The Capital is dark and you can see only a short way.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: You move more slowly.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: The service-tunnel network is down: no travel.

speaker: (narration)
current_text: Healing items do not work (food does not agree with the Capital).
